location: England, specifically Liverpool and surrounding areas
institution: London and West Coast Railway Company and local police
crime_subtype: vanishing of a special train by diversion and concealment

cast.name: James McPherson
behavioral_tells: wrote letter to wife revealing secrets

cast.name: William Smith
cast.private_secret: bribed to assist in train diversion

surface_summary: A special train carrying Monsieur Caratal and his companion mysteriously vanished between Kenyon Junction and Barton Moss. The engine-driver was found dead nearby, but no trace of the train or passengers was discovered, baffling investigators and the public alike.
accepted_facts: The special train left Liverpool on time and was seen passing several stations.
The engine-driver John Slater was found dead with head injuries near the line.
No trace of the train or its carriages was found on the railway line.
A letter from the missing guard James McPherson was received from New York.
inferred_conclusions: The train ran off the rails and crashed unnoticed.
The train was submerged in a nearby canal.
The train was destroyed by a novel explosive device.
mechanism_description: The special train was secretly diverted onto an abandoned side line connected to an unused mine shaft. The train was run at high speed into the shaft, causing it to crash and be destroyed. The conspirators removed all evidence by dismantling the temporary rails and covering the shaft, effectively making the train vanish without a trace.
delivery_path: Preparation of a side line by laying temporary rails to the abandoned Heartsease mine.
Bribing of railway staff including the guard and stoker to assist in the plan.
The special train is switched onto the side line without the passengers noticing.
The train is driven at full speed into the mine shaft, crashing and destroying it.
The conspirators remove the temporary rails and cover the mine shaft to conceal the wreckage.
The guard and stoker escape before the crash, while the engine-driver is killed during the attempt to chloroform him.
The conspirators disperse and cover their tracks, including sending a false letter from the guard.
outcome_result: The special train and its passengers disappeared without a trace, with the true cause revealed only by the confession of Herbert de Lernac years later.

false_assumption.statement: The train must have derailed or crashed somewhere visible along the main line.
false_assumption.why_it_seems_reasonable: The train was seen passing stations and the engine-driver was found dead nearby, suggesting an accident on the main line. No other plausible location was known for the disappearance.
false_assumption.what_it_hides: The train was diverted onto a hidden abandoned side line and destroyed in a concealed mine shaft, making it invisible to observers on the main line.

supporting_points: He was found to have written a letter to his wife revealing secrets.
He was the guard on the missing special train.
His behavior was suspicious and he fled to America.
He was bribed by conspirators to assist in the crime.
false_solution.the_one_flaw: He was only an accomplice and not the mastermind; the real plan was orchestrated by Herbert de Lernac.

red_herrings.description: The suggestion that the train ran off the rails and sank in the nearby canal.
red_herrings.innocent_explanation: The canal was too shallow to conceal the train and no wreckage was found there.

red_herrings.description: The theory that a novel explosive device destroyed the train completely.
red_herrings.innocent_explanation: The metals of the train remained undamaged and no explosion evidence was found.

closed_circle.rationale: All had access to the train and were involved in its operation; the conspiracy required insiders to divert and destroy the train.

time_windows: Train must disappear between Kenyon Junction and Barton Moss

inference_path.observation: No special train passed Barton Moss station.
inference_path.correction: The train must have left the main line before Barton Moss.
inference_path.effect: Focus on possible side lines between Kenyon Junction and Barton Moss.
required_evidence: Telegram from Barton Moss station denying special train passage
Railway maps showing side lines in the area

inference_path.observation: The line between Kenyon Junction and Barton Moss has no siding.
inference_path.correction: Investigate abandoned or disconnected side lines nearby.
inference_path.effect: Consider possibility of temporary rails laid on abandoned lines.
required_evidence: Inspection reports of abandoned side lines
Statements from railway workers about temporary rails

inference_path.observation: The engine-driver John Slater was found dead near the line.
inference_path.correction: He was likely incapacitated during the diversion.
inference_path.effect: Suggest foul play involving driver to enable train diversion.

inference_path.observation: Guard James McPherson wrote a letter from New York.
inference_path.correction: He fled after the crime, indicating involvement.
inference_path.effect: Identify him as an accomplice or conspirator.
required_evidence: Letter from James McPherson to his wife

inference_path.observation: Temporary rails were laid to connect the side line to the main line.
inference_path.correction: The train could be diverted onto the abandoned line.
inference_path.effect: Train disappearance explained by diversion and crash in mine shaft.
required_evidence: Physical evidence of rails and points

inference_path.observation: The train was not seen by workers on the Perseverance Colliery line.
inference_path.correction: Train passed through quickly or unnoticed due to speed and location.
inference_path.effect: Supports theory of diversion onto hidden side line.

inference_path.observation: Confession of Herbert de Lernac detailing the plan.
inference_path.correction: Confession confirms the diversion and destruction of the train.
inference_path.effect: Final confirmation of the true mechanism of the crime.

discriminating_test.design: Reconstruct the diversion by laying temporary rails on the abandoned side line and running a test train to observe if it can be diverted unnoticed. Observe the visibility from the main line and the reaction of workers along the side line.
discriminating_test.knowledge_revealed: This test reveals the feasibility of diverting a train onto the abandoned line without detection and the possibility of the train disappearing into the mine shaft.
discriminating_test.pass_condition: The test train must be successfully diverted onto the side line and reach the mine shaft without being seen or stopped by workers on the main line.

fair_play_explanation: The reader is provided with detailed information about the railway lines, the timing of the train's passage, the existence of abandoned side lines, and the suspicious behavior of railway staff. The confession and the telegrams give clues that the train was diverted. The physical impossibility of the train being on the main line after Barton Moss invites the reader to consider hidden tracks and sabotage. The presence of bribed staff and the discovery of the engine-driver's body provide further hints. All these clues are available before the solution is revealed.
